labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE (de-bridged): VICE runs on the host, headless, no QEMU/QMP, no guest OS, no X, no exec channel. Frames VICE_SHM_PATH->shm (the same IFB1 wire format drawshm uses), keys vicectl + the shared us-layout keysym table, audio -sounddev wav -> FIFO. Launcher stations/vice-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the checkpoint in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/c64/sta/golden.vsf. KEYBOARD-ONLY: the bridged station's COMM 1351 mouse is NOT wired on this path — vice_sock.rs and vicectl both lack a pointer verb — so drive GEOS with labctl type/key and read it with labctl shot.

render.stationsManifestPrelude:
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GROUP G — emulator-bridge retro home computers (c64, atarist, apple2, amiga).
#   Each tile is a captured Debian 12 "bridge" kiosk (shared read-only base
#   /data/vms/bridge/bridge-base.qcow2 + a thin per-tile overlay.qcow2) running
#   a period emulator full-screen; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer +
#   AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and
#   docs/guests/c64.md. Atari ST/Apple II/Amiga use usb-tablet ABS; C64 keeps
#   browser coordinates absolute but streamhost translates them to PS/2 REL for
#   VICE's SDL/1351 path (vmport=off, no tablet). All four use AC97, KVM,
#   -m 1536 -smp 2 -cpu host -vga std. VERBATIM LAUNCHERS: overlay.qcow2 (ide,
#   holds the INTERNAL golden snapshot — NEVER delete), e1000 NIC with an ssh
#   hostfwd (c64:5814 atarist:5816 apple2:5817 amiga:5818 -> guest :22), and a
#   CONDITIONAL -loadvm golden. station.env carries the golden-fixture stanza
#   (SH_RESET_MODE=loadvm etc.) via the tracked fixture files.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# c64 (VMID 214) — VICE x64sc -> Commodore 64 -> GEOS 2.0 deskTop. ssh 5814.

museum.blurb: A full windows-icons-menus desktop (GEOS) running on a 1 MHz, 64 KB home computer — the 8-bit era’s answer to the Macintosh.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 12 kiosk runs VICE (x64sc) full-screen emulating a C64 that auto-boots the GEOS 2.0 deskTop; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio (the C64 SID routed through ALSA) exactly like every other tile. archetype beige-tower-crt (ideal: a bespoke C64 breadbin + 1541 + CRT). See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md. HOST-NATIVE SINCE 2026-08-17 (de-bridging campaign): VICE x64sc runs on the host, headless — no QEMU, no guest Debian, no X — and the scene is restored from a VICE checkpoint rather than a QEMU snapshot. ONE CAPABILITY IS NOT BACK YET: the bridged exhibit had a COMM 1351 mouse on control port 1, and the host-native input path has no pointer verb at all, so this station is KEYBOARD-ONLY for now and the registry declares pointer.present false. GEOS still runs; it is driven from the keyboard. Wiring the mouse is scoped follow-up work (the browser sends absolute coordinates, the 1351 is a proportional device VICE drives from relative host motion). The prose above still describes the retired bridge tile and is rewritten with the other nine.
